Amaury Diaz Serrano.bio: Amaury Diaz Serrano is a Puerto Rican-American industrial designer who was one of the six designers who participated in the Hot Wheels Designers Challenge; he represented General Motors's Chevrolet division, for he was Senior Industrial Designer, by designing the Chevroletor for said series, initially known as "Prototype 40". Diaz Serrano's dream was apparently to design a Hot Wheels car since he was a child. Diaz Serrano joined GM in 1999, working on numerous designs such as the exterior design of the Cadillac Sixteen; he left in 2015 and currently manages his own firm, Amaury Diaz Serrano Industrial Design LLC, as well as running Jigxocars, his other design firm.

Blake Allen.bio: David Blake Allen is a former Hot Wheels designer who designed cars for Mattel in 2004 as one of three external designers who designed cars for Hot Wheels. Prior to his leadership position, Blake attended Western Hills High School from 1987-1989. In 1999, he completed his Bachelor of Science in Industrial Design from the University of Cincinnati. He currently works as a Senior Lead Designer at General Motors, a position he has held since 2010. Blake Allen was a former classmate of Eric Tscherne.

Bob Lovejoy.bio: Robert B. Lovejoy was a Hot Wheels designer who designed Hot Wheels from 1971 to 1973. He was hired alongside Larry Wood and Paul Tam as one of their earliest designers; he was most known for his work on the RRRumblers. Outside of work, Lovejoy was an aircraft enthusiast, building his own aircraft and gliders, most notably the Quicksilver; after he left Mattel he turned to solely developing aircraft and hang gliders. By 1980, he had an ultralight aircraft design penned out; he tested the aircraft in late 1982, but due to a control failure the aircraft crashed and he was unfortunately killed in the process.

Bob Rosas.bio: Robert Raymond Rosas is a former Hot Wheels designer and engineer who worked for Mattel from 1969 to 1989. He is known to have worked alongside Larry Wood in the design department, designing and innovating for various Hot Wheels series. He worked his way up to become the director of the Hot Wheels engineering group before leaving Mattel entirely in 1989. Many of the innovative series such as X-V Racers, Steering Rigs, Crack-Ups, Flip Outs and the like can all be attributed to Rosas's work. He is currently retired, although his relationship with Hot Wheels's Design Team remains healthy, frequently attending conventions.

Bruce Baur.bio: Bruce Alden Baur is a former Hot Wheels designer who was employed by Mattel from 1987 to 2002. He designed castings from at least 1993 to 1997, as well as doing work for the Collectibles line. His best known designs are Power Pipes, Rigor Motor, Silhouette II, Splittin' Image II, Twin Mill II (1993), Shadow Jet II, Way 2 Fast, Twang Thang and Lexus SC400. He was noted to have been good friends with Phil Riehlman, and was noted as the creator of the 100% Hot Wheels line as well as the 4-Car sets. After leaving Mattel, he worked for Mechanix Wear and competing brand Spin Master and was last known to be an in-house design consultant for an Indonesian coachbuilder company, Morodadi Prima. He is currently retired.

Chris Colangelo.bio: Christopher R. Colangelo is a Hot Wheels designer who has been working with Mattel since 2013. He is the design lead on the Hot Wheels Mario Kart series vehicles, Star Wars playsets, the Star Wars Starships line, design lead on San Diego Comic-Con exclusives and has worked on other major licenses for Hot Wheels, such as DC. Prior to his career at Mattel, he worked at Wham-O Toys, Jakks Pacific and Crayola and also had an internship career at Mattel before his full-time career.

Dave Deal.bio: David Allen Deal, nicknamed Big Deal, was an independent American illustrator who worked with Mattel in 2003, likely as a subcontractor. Born in 1938, Deal studied graphic design in Louisiana Tech University before becoming an illustrator for the Dallas Morning News; outside of that Deal was a notable illustrator, illustrating automobiles with "exaggerated" proportions, such as the Deal's Wheels model kit line for Revell. Deal also set a record in a specially-modified Volkswagen Beetle on a 1000-mile route from Tijuana to La Paz alongside then-Revell product manager Don Ernst. Deal passed away on 14 October 2008, aged 70, due to health problems; one of his last projects was concept art for the movie Cars.

Dave Martis.bio: David A. Martis is a Hot Wheels designer, modelmaker, and prototyper who worked with Mattel from 1999 to late 2004 as a senior project designer and model maker. Known for his work on Mechanix, Robo Wheels, Gyro Jets, IR Rally, and 1/64 scale Disney/Pixar Cars prototypes, he preferred casting and hand painting "B-grade" resins using clay, SLA 3D prints, and existing parts from around the model shop as the process was "quicker and easier" than sketching concept art. It was stated by Eric Tscherne that his work features varying imperfections based off of the importance or purpose of each piece. He enjoyed casting and often made personal pieces that "blurred the line" between employee custom and prototype; many of his projects were used in presentations or eventual production releases. Many are marked with "X3008" on their bases; the "X" stood for "eXtension" to his office number "3008" to ensure their proper return after use. In years prior Martis designed bikes for GT Bicycles and automotive accessories for Powers Design International. After his tenure he worked at fellow toy company Playmates for a year, later founding his own company, Devium Design.

Dave Sheltman.bio: David Alan Sheltman is a former Mattel employee who worked with Mattel from at least 1999 to about 2017. He was originally part of Hot Wheels's Innovation and Track groups, as well as working on "whatever needed his special attention". Mainly working on track sets and playsets, he also designed cars but not very often. After his stint at Hot Wheels he then moved to Matchbox to design various large scale vehicles and other non-diecast projects, such as Wrecky the Wrecking Buddy. Sheltman left Mattel around 2017; he currently works for Spin Master.

Felix Holst.bio: Felix C. Holst is a British designer who worked with Mattel's Hot Wheels division from 2004 to 2015 as the vice president of the creative division. A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, Holst came to the United States some time after graduation and joined Mattel. He left Mattel in 2015 to found Hackrod Inc., a company specializing in vehicle design, which appears to have since closed. He is currently self-employed and is the founder of Holst Automotive; on the side, plays the bass guitar with a band called The Kustom Built and is a painter.

Fraser Campbell.bio: Fraser Lee Campbell is a British Hot Wheels designer who worked at Mattel from 1998 to 2016 and again since 2021. Initially based in the UK, Fraser moved to the United States in 2000 to join the Hot Wheels design team; his first design was the Maelstrom. He would move to Hong Kong at some point later before moving back to the United States; much of his work during his time at Mattel involved designing for Monster Jam and various haulers. Campbell left Mattel in early 2016 to join Hackrod. He left Hackrod in mid-2020 and returned to Mattel in 2021 as Lead Project designer for Basics/Mainline.

Gary Ragle.bio: Gary Ragle is an American automotive designer who was one of the six designers who participated in the Hot Wheels Designers Challenge; he represented Mitsubishi Motors, for he was Senior Designer for Mitsubishi Motors R&D of America, by designing the Mitsubishi Double Shotz for said series. Ragle joined Mitsubishi R&D initially as an intern in 2002 before transitioning to a full-time role and leaving in 2009, and is one of two Designers Challenge designers with ties to Hot Wheels before going onto professional design; he interned at Mattel in 2000. He currently runs his own design firm, Ragle Design, as well as designing for Hydra Design Labs, an automotive design consultancy.

Harald Belker.bio: Harald Georg Belker is a German industrial designer who worked for Mattel from 2004 to 2006 as a design consultant. Born in Krefeld in 1961, Belker is noted for his futuristic automobile designs, such as the Lexus 2054 from the film Minority Report, the Batmobile from Batman & Robin and the Hover Car from Total Recall. He currently manages his own design firm, Harald Belker Design and designs vehicles for the movie industry on a part-time basis; he is also noted to have been employed on a contractural basis by Apple, Waymo and Samsung.

Harry Bradley.bio: Harry Bentley Bradley was an American automotive designer who is often considered the father of Hot Wheels designs; as Hot Wheels's very first designer, he created the original "Sweet 16" cars of 1968. Bradley worked for Mattel from 1966 to 1969. Born in Boston in 1936, Bradley suffered polio from a young age; despite this, he nurtured his talents drawing automobiles and continued sketching in hospitals as he received treatment for his condition. Prior to working for Hot Wheels, Bradley worked for General Motors, having been recruited in 1962, as well as being a builder of his own show cars such as the La Jolla, Blind Faith and the Deora. Bradley was recruited by Mattel in 1966, who wanted a designer from one of the Big 3 automakers to help design their vehicles. Bradley drove his 1964 Chevrolet El Camino to California; it is said that Mattel founder Elliot Handler saw Bradley's El Camino in the parking lot and quipped "Those are some hot wheels." Bradley's ties with GM were pivotal to the creation of some of the earliest Hot Wheels models. Lore has it that to design one of these GM models, the Custom Corvette, Bradley drove to Detroit in 1967 and snuck into GM's offices after working hours. Having worked in GM's design offices in the past, he was able to locate the area where the design blueprints were stored; he would take the blueprints for the upcoming 1968 Corvette by hiding them in his crutches, then drive back to California where he designed the model off those blueprints. Due to this it is often claimed the Hot Wheels version of the Corvette came out before the actual Corvette hit dealerships, much to GM's consternation, although various dating of prototypes and the corroboration of other dates states that this might not have been the case. Regardless, the Corvette was a highly popular model and caused great publicity for Mattel. Bradley left Mattel in 1969. The story behind how he left varies; some sources say he felt Hot Wheels would not take off and as such left the brand thinking it would only be a fad, while other sources say he was fired due to his refusal to be reassigned to the staples division of Mattel, with his manager fully convinced that the Hot Wheels line would fail. Others state that his firing might have been related to the aforementioned stunt he pulled regarding the Custom Corvette if indeed he did pull it off. This thought about failure held true for a time as Hot Wheels as a brand was not making any money with Mattel many a time considering retiring the brand and making numerous changes to cut costs, although in retrospect, he should have stayed and continued designing as the brand began turning a profit quickly during the mid 1970s. Prior to leaving Mattel, he recommended his friend Ira Gilford for the position, which the latter accepted. After leaving Mattel, Bradley started a design firm and did work on a number of projects. He then went on to become a lecturer at the Art Central College of Design, the institute from which many future Hot Wheels designers would graduate; he would also sporadically design new cars, with one of the last cars he did around the tail end of his "active period" being his "shark fin" 1993 Infiniti J30, although his last project was apparently a Pontiac he did for a friend circa 2010. Bradley passed away on 13 May 2023, aged 86.

Howard Rees.bio: Howard K. Rees is a former Hot Wheels designer who worked at Mattel from 1969 to 1975. Prior to his work at Mattel, he accepted a position at Ford of Europe. Rees left the Hot Wheels design team in 1971 to design the Major Matt Mason action figures, recommending a friend of his named Larry Wood to the position. Rees left Mattel entirely in 1975 and became a painter, which he still is to this day.

Ira Gilford.bio: Ira Bailey Gilford is a former Hot Wheels designer who worked at Mattel from 1967 to 1970. He is most known for designing a large number of the 1969 cars, The Spoilers, The Heavys and most notably, the Twin Mill, Hot Wheels's first original design. Prior to working for Mattel, Gilford worked for the Chrysler Corporation. Gilford was recommended to the position by his friend Harry Bradley, Hot Wheels's first designer. Gilford left Mattel around 1970. He currently works as an independent contractor in the digital arts field and a painter.

Jason Hill.bio: Jason C. Hill is an automotive designer who worked for Mattel around 2005, likely on a subcontractor basis. He is the founder of Eleven, an automotive design consultancy, which he has run since 2003. Prior to his work at Eleven, Hill worked for Hyundai, Porsche and ill-fated automotive company Aptera Motors as a designer; he was also the lead designer of the Porsche Carrera GT Concept showcased in 2000, working alongside noted automotive designer Harm Lagaay.

John Reale.bio: John Packard Reale is a former Mattel employee who worked with Mattel from 1995 to 2006. He helped diversify and expand the Hot Wheels lineup by creating and innovating a play pattern segmentation roadmap, and is credited as being one of the brainchilds for Mattel's highly-successful Pixar Cars diecast lineup. Reale worked for competing brand Hasbro as Vice President of Design and Development from 2010 to 2020, and currently works as a Chief Product Officer at BEGiN, overseeing Little Passports.

Jun Imai.bio: Jun Imai is a Japanese-American former Hot Wheels designer who worked at Mattel from 2004 to 2018. Although his designs include classic American muscle cars and fantasy cars, he is most known for his Japanese cars. He has made replicas of his own 1:1 vehicles; the '71 Datsun Bluebird 510 Wagon, the Nissan Fairlady Z and the Datsun 620. He left Mattel in 2018; he currently acts as the creative director of Kaido House, a company he founded selling automotive enthusiast merchandise and later morphing into a line of highly-detailed diecast cars manufactured in collaboration with TrueScale Miniatures and marketed as a subline to their Mini GT product line. His Kaido House brand also appeared on various Hot Wheels cars and he maintains a good relationship with his ex-colleagues.

Lindsey Lee.bio: Lindsey Eun-ji Leeis a Korean Hot Wheels designer who worked with Mattel from 2016 to 2022; she is notable as being Hot Wheels's first full-time female designer. This was her first job after graduating from the Art Center College of Design in 2015; prior to that, she interned at the Nissan Headquarter Studios in Tokyo. At Mattel she designed mainly formainline,Premiumand Extensions, as well as being in charge of designing retools for existing castings. After Hot Wheels she relocated back to South Korea and works in the fashion industry, acting as a design lead for the New Era Cap Company.

Miguel López.bio: Miguel Angel López Jr.is a Spanish-American Hot Wheels designer who worked at Mattel from 2012 to 2015, designing cars for both the Hot Wheels andMatchboxlines. He designed Hot Wheels cars such as theFast 4WDandX-Steam, as well as a number of Star Wars and Disney Character Cars. He is currently a freelance artist, having been one since leaving Mattel, with his notable works now being a number of vehicles for thePaw Patrolline of toys manufactured by competing brand Spin Master. In addition to his work as an artist, López also worked as an English teacher from 2015 to 2017, first in Madrid, Spain and then later in Tokyo, Japan. He is currently based in Japan.

Mike Nuttall.bio: Michael Wayne Nuttallis a former Hot Wheels designer who worked at Mattel's Hot Wheels division from 1999 to 2016; he mostly worked on designing track and playsets but occasionally designed vehicles, with his development on track sets leading him to be dubbed "Track Master Mike". He is decribed as "a master of toy design", he is stated to be able to whip out a "great concept sketch" faster than most people can pick up their pen. He is currently a member of InvenToy, a company started by former Hot Wheels engineersEric OstendorffandKeith Hippely. Prior to his stint at Hot Wheels, he worked for Mattel's Preschool division from 1970 to 1978 before moving to competing brand Tomy.

Nathan Proch.bio: Nathan Clifford Prochis a former designer for Hot Wheels who worked at Mattel from 1993 to 2006; around that time he became debilitated with an unspecified illness which prevented him from working full time, and left soon after. Before his illness, Proch was responsible for the creation of theCM5wheel and the cut-out logos that appeared on the bases of Hot Wheels cars from 2005 to 2006. He also acted as Director of Hot Wheels Design for a time. Proch was inducted into the Diecast Hall of Fame in 2014 but declined the award; he has since kept a low profile.

Omar Rehman.bio: Omar Nayeemur Rehmanis a former Hot Wheels designer who interned at Mattel from June to December 2017. He designed both vehicles and smaller playsets. Prior to working at Mattel, Rehman interned at The Carlab and was PR for EuroJet Racing; after his stint at Hot Wheels he interned at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory and worked as an industrial designer on contract with studio.VO and MODUS Group. He was last a communication designer for D-Ford, the Ford Motor Company's human-centric design group. He can be found on the internet under the handle @youknowitsomar.

Otto Kuhni.biografia_limpia: Otto Johnson Kuhni was a graphic artist that designed many the early art work for blisterpacks, cases and sets. Born in 1927 in Utah the fourth of five children, Kuhni began work as a freelance artist in 1962 and began
Otto Kuhni.bio: Otto Johnson Kuhniwas a graphic artist that designed many the early art work for blisterpacks, cases and sets. Born in 1927 in Utah the fourth of five children, Kuhni began work as a freelance artist in 1962 and began work with Mattel in 1967 after being hired byRick Irons, doing many of the drawings for card art and playsets; he even designed some large playsets himself. Kuhni retired in 1995, but returned part-time to do artwork for the then-newHot Wheels Collectorsseries of cars, the accompanyingRed Line Cluband various other retro-themed products. Kuhni died in 2017, aged 90; his legacy lives in the form of his artwork as well as theCustom Otto, a rendition of the generic car he drew for the 1968 packaging artwork that was ultimately never released in the line and named in his honor.

Phil Riehlman.bio: Philip Oscar Riehlmanis a Hot Wheels designer that has been designing Hot Wheels cars since 1993. His first designs were theTwin Mill IIand theSilhouette IIas collaborations withBruce Baur; he also designed briefly for sister line Matchbox and currently also serves as a senior manager of Mattel. He was lead designer for theHot Wheels idline prior to its cancelation and currently designs models for Premium and the mainline; he is the lead designer forPremium 1:43andElite 64. He initially worked as an intern in 1991 before applying for a permanent position at the Male Action Figures department in 1993; he was subsequently transferred back to the Hot Wheels department, where he has been ever since.

Rob Matthes.bio: Robert William Matthesis a designer who worked at Hot Wheels from 2002 to 2017 and again since2023. He served as a design manager for Hot Wheels from 2008 to 2017, managing the $1 lineup from 2008 to2012as well as being the design lead for theHot Wheels Eliteand 1:50 scale lines and then managed the playset team until his departure in 2017. He also manages his own company, SpeedShift Art, specializing in automotive illustration. He rejoined Hot Wheels in 2023, working mainly onPremiumproducts and currently manages theFormula One CollectionandRacing Culturelines.

Ryu Asada.bio: Ryu Asada was a Japanese Hot Wheels designer who worked at Mattel from 2004 to 2021 and oversaw the design of cars in the basic $1 mainline lineup as a Designer Project Lead, taking over from Jun Imai. Born in Osaka, he pursued a degree at the Art Center College of Design after emigrating to the United States. After graduating, he initially began work as a designer for Matchbox from 2004 to 2012; he first designed for Hot Wheels in 2009 as a "guest designer", and would join the Hot Wheels design team three years later. He passed away on 23 March 2021 at the age of 42 from cancer. A mini-segment of the 2022 mainline, dubbed Ryu's Rides, as well as the Ryu Asada Award for the 2021 Hot Wheels Legends Tour, were both created to celebrate his life and to honor his legacy.

Sei Cho.bio: Sei Chois a former Hot Wheels designer who worked with Mattel from 2004 to 2006. Originally working with Jada Toys, he left the company in 2004 to join Mattel, where he worked for two years; while at Hot Wheels, Sei worked at the Hot Wheels "Trend" Group alongsideJun Imaito design "unconventional body styles" for Hot Wheels models, such as the Drop Tops and Blings models, stating that "essential line" vehicles (i.e. Realistix) were "a special treat". He also worked onDropstars,Dropstars Urban Assault Vehicles,Custom Classics,Hot Import NightsandHIN D-Forcemodels. After leaving Mattel in 2006, he worked with a number of industrial design firms before he rejoined Jada Toys in 2016, where he currently serves as a design manager.

Steve Moran.bio: Steven M. Moranis a former Hot Wheels designer who worked at the company from 1997 to 2011. Moran was first asked to direct the Hong Kong Hot Wheels design team in 1997, and became a senior design manager in 2000. He worked with Hot Wheels mainly managing the direction of the Hot Wheels Elite line among other lines and left the design team in 2008 to work for another division of Mattel. Moran left Mattel entirely in 2011 and went to work for Jada Toys; he also founded Moran Devices LLC the same year. Moran returned to Mattel as a "mentor project lead" in 2012 and left in 2015.

Terry Choy.bio: Terence Allan Choywas a Chinese-American toy designer who designed for Mattel from1984to 2005. He started as Senior Designer (1984-1985), Project Designer (1985-1987), then Senior Project Designer (1988-2005). He was the Project Manager for the Adult/Collector Division of Hot Wheels Racing, which included Formula 1, NASCAR and Rally products. He was responsible for the earliest Batmobile casting designs for Hot Wheels with the 100% Batmobiles Series which debuted in 2003 with the Dream Halloween 1989 Batmobile; made for charity. He was a designer forThe Simpsonstoy line in addition to his Hot Wheels portfolio. He was one of the designers for some of the vehicles for an ill-fatedHe Manmovie, alongside a number of other Hot Wheels designers. Terry passed away on 7 April 2020 from cancer, aged 67.

Tyler Charest.bio: Tyler J. Charest is a Hot Wheels designer who has worked at Mattel since 2015, where he currently serves as a lead designer; he was a Hot Wheels designer from 2015 to 2020. Prior to his work at Mattel, he developed concepts for Toyota Boshoku America and worked as an industrial designer; he also interned at Mattel for three months as an "innovation design intern" in 2014 before joining Mattel full-time. He currently works as associate manager of the Matchbox design team.

Wayne Scott.bio: Wayne Arthur Scott Jr.was a Hot Wheels designer who worked for Mattel from 1997 to 2009. He was mainly a graphic designer, with his name appearing on numerous castings as a sponsor decal; in addition to graphics, Scott also designed castings but not in large volumes. Prior to his stint at Mattel, Scott did graphics for Revell's NASCAR model kits. He passed away on 26 March 2017, aged 45; a cause of death was not announced.

York Bleyer.bio: York H. Bleyeris a former Hot Wheels designer and design manager who worked at Mattel from 2007 to 2011. Prior to working at Mattel, he was an industrial designer, working with numerous companies before moving to Mattel in 2007. Initially working with Tyco, York moved to Hot Wheels in 2011 where he managed various employees and led the Innovation Small Vehicles and Track and Playsets team, in addition to contributing to some design work. Projects he contributed to during his tenure at Hot Wheels includeStealth Rides,Wall Tracks, Batman, Cars, Toy Story, Green Lantern,Speed Racerand Max Steel playsets. After his tenure at Mattel he worked for Ridemakerz and ran his own design studio, and was last an adjunct professor at the Academy of Art University. Driving through the streets of San Francisco provided its challenges but confirmed his belief that a motorcycle was the perfect tool for commuting in the city. He has used this form of transportation for commuting to work in New York City, Detroit and Troy Michigan to the greater Los Angeles Southern California area. Riding bikes has remained his favorite way to travel to this day.
